34108.q: What do you call people who move away from a municipality?
34108.e: Someone who leaves a municipality and lives elsewhere is moving away. The opposite is a newcomer.
34108.m: Someone who leaves is moving away.

34110.q: Who do you give your new address to after moving so that letters arrive correctly?
34110.e: The post office needs to know where to deliver the letters. You can tell it your new address, and then it forwards your letters.
34110.m: After moving, you tell the post office your new address.

34111.q: Which school do newcomers' children usually go to?
a: The school where they now live
34111.e: Children usually go to school where they live. After moving, they attend the school of the new municipality.
34111.m: Children go to school where they now live.

34112.q: How can newcomers quickly get to know new people in the village?
34112.e: In clubs you meet people with the same hobbies. That way newcomers quickly make contacts.
34112.m: In a club, you quickly get to know new people.

34113.q: When may adult Swiss newcomers vote in their new municipality?
a: As soon as they have registered
34113.e: Swiss voters may vote where they live. To do so, they must be registered there.
34113.m: Anyone who is registered may vote where they live.

34114.q: What do newcomers often bring to a village?
34114.e: New people bring experience from other places with them. That brings new ideas into village life.

34115.q: What is it called when two municipalities become one?
34115.e: In a municipal merger, two or more municipalities join together. After that there is only one municipality.
34115.m: In a municipal merger, municipalities become one.

34116.q: Who usually decides whether municipalities merge?
34116.e: The voters of the municipalities involved vote on a merger. So they have a say.
34116.m: The voters vote on a municipal merger.

34117.q: What happens to the number of municipalities after a merger?
34117.e: Several municipalities become one. So afterwards there are fewer municipalities.
34117.m: After a merger there are fewer municipalities.

34118.q: Which canton merged its many municipalities into just three in 2011?
34118.e: In the canton of Glarus, the 25 municipalities were merged into three in 2011. They are called Glarus, Glarus Nord and Glarus Süd.
34118.m: Since 2011 the canton of Glarus has had only three municipalities.

34119.q: What does a new municipality often get after a merger?
34119.e: After a merger the new municipality needs a name. Sometimes it gets a completely new one, sometimes it keeps an old one.
34119.m: A merged municipality often gets a new name.

34120.q: Why do small municipalities often merge?
a: To do their jobs better together
To get more seats in the National Council
So they no longer charge taxes
34120.e: Small municipalities sometimes find it hard to get people for the official posts. Together they can do their jobs better.
34120.m: Small municipalities merge to be stronger together.

34121.q: What still remains after a municipal merger?
34121.e: The houses and villages stay where they are. Only the administration is combined.
34121.m: After a merger the villages remain.

34122.q: On which day does a new, merged municipality usually begin?
34122.e: Municipal mergers usually take effect at the start of a year. That way the new municipality can start with its own budget.
34122.m: Merged municipalities usually start on 1 January.

34123.q: What is a gathering called where a municipality welcomes new residents?
34123.e: Many municipalities invite people who have just moved there to a newcomers' welcome event. There they are made to feel welcome.
34123.m: At the newcomers' welcome event the municipality greets new residents.

34124.q: Who is invited to a newcomers' welcome event?
a: People who have just moved there
34124.e: The people invited are those who have recently moved to the municipality. They can often bring their family.
34124.m: New residents are invited to the newcomers' welcome event.

34125.q: What do newcomers learn about at a newcomers' welcome event?
34125.e: The municipality introduces itself and shows what the village has to offer. That helps new people find their way around.
34125.m: At the newcomers' welcome event you get to know your new municipality.

34126.q: Who often greets the guests at a newcomers' welcome event?
34126.e: The mayor, who is the president of the municipality, often gives a short speech. That way the newcomers get to know the authorities.
34126.m: The mayor often speaks at the newcomers' welcome event.

34127.q: What is often served at the end of a newcomers' welcome event?
34127.e: After the speeches there is often something to drink and eat. During this apéro people can chat with each other.
34127.m: After the newcomers' welcome event there are often drinks and snacks.

34128.q: Who else often introduces themselves at a newcomers' welcome event?
34128.e: Clubs show what they do at the event. That way newcomers quickly find a hobby that suits them.
34128.m: The clubs often introduce themselves at the newcomers' welcome event.

34129.q: What is the aim of a newcomers' welcome event?
34129.e: New residents should feel at home in the village. So the municipality gives them a friendly welcome.
34129.m: The newcomers' welcome event welcomes new people.

34130.q: What do some municipalities do with the guests at a newcomers' welcome event?
34130.e: On a walk the newcomers are shown important places in the village. These include the school and the municipal offices, for example.
34130.m: A walk round the village shows newcomers the important places.

34131.q: What is the club called where people sing together?
34131.e: In a choir, lots of people sing songs together. Many villages have a church choir or a men's or women's choir.
34131.m: In a choir people sing together.

34132.q: In which village club do people play brass band music?
34132.e: The village band plays brass band music, for example at village festivals. Many villages have their own band.
34132.m: The village band plays brass band music.

34133.q: What is the club called where people do gymnastics together?
34133.e: In a gymnastics club people do sport and exercises together. Many gymnastics clubs have a group for children.
34133.m: In a gymnastics club people do gymnastics together.

34134.q: What is the person called who leads a club?
34134.e: The president leads the club. He or she chairs the meetings.

34135.q: Who looks after the money in a club?
34135.e: The treasurer manages the club's money. He or she writes down all the income and spending.
34135.m: The treasurer manages the money in a club.

34136.q: What do members usually pay to a club every year?
34136.e: With the membership fees the club pays for things like equipment or courses. They are usually paid once a year.

34137.q: What are the rules a club writes down called?
34137.e: Every club has statutes. They say, for example, what the club is for and how decisions are made.
34137.m: A club's rules are called its statutes.

34138.q: What is the meeting of all a club's members called?
34138.e: All the members meet at the general meeting. There they elect the committee, for example.
34138.m: All club members meet at the general meeting.

34139.q: Which village club helps with first aid when there are accidents?
34139.e: Samaritans learn first aid. They help out at festivals and sports events, for example.
34139.m: The Samaritan association helps with first aid.

34140.q: What is the festival called when decorated cows come down from the Alpine pasture to the village in autumn?
34140.e: In autumn the herders bring the cattle back from the Alpine pasture to the valley. The cows wear flowers and bells, and the village celebrates.
34140.m: At the Alpine descent the decorated cows come back from the Alpine pasture.

34141.q: Where is a village festival often held when it rains?
34141.e: For big festivals, clubs often put up a festival tent. Everyone stays dry inside, even when it rains.
34141.m: At a village festival you stay dry in the festival tent.

34142.q: What is a village fair with rides and market stalls in autumn often called?
34142.e: The Chilbi is a traditional fair with a merry-go-round, stalls and food. Many villages celebrate it once a year.
34142.m: The Chilbi is a village fair with rides and stalls.

34143.q: Who often helps so that a village festival can take place?
34143.e: Clubs set up stalls, cook and sell things. They often use the money to fill their club funds.
34143.m: Clubs often help with the village festival.

34144.q: What do people carry through the village in the turnip lantern parade?
34144.e: For the turnip lantern parade, children carve patterns into turnips. A light burns inside, and everyone walks through the village with them.
34144.m: In the turnip lantern parade you carry a glowing turnip.

34145.q: What is a village festival good for?
34145.e: At a village festival young and old come together. That way you get to know the people in the village better.
34145.m: At the village festival the people of the village meet.

34146.q: What is the place at a festival called where you can eat and drink?
34146.e: In the food and drink area, clubs sell food and drinks. People sit together there at long tables.
34146.m: In the food and drink area you can eat and drink at the festival.

34147.q: What is the winter festival called where people dress up and wear masks?
34147.e: At carnival lots of people dress up and wear masks. There are parades with Guggenmusik bands.
34147.m: At carnival people dress up and wear masks.

34148.q: What is a club for the people of one part of a town called?
34148.e: Towns have many neighbourhoods. In the neighbourhood association the residents work for their neighbourhood.
34148.m: The neighbourhood association works for its neighbourhood.

34149.e: A town is divided into several neighbourhoods. Each neighbourhood has its own streets and squares.
34149.m: A neighbourhood is a part of a town.

34150.q: What does a neighbourhood association often organise?
34150.e: Many neighbourhood associations organise parties, flea markets or outings. That way the neighbours get to know each other.
34150.m: The neighbourhood association often organises a neighbourhood party.

34151.q: Who does the neighbourhood association tell what the neighbourhood is missing?
a: The school in the next village
34151.e: The neighbourhood association passes on the residents' wishes to the town authorities. For example, a safe zebra crossing.
34151.m: The neighbourhood association takes wishes to the town.

34152.q: Who can usually take part in the neighbourhood association?
34152.e: Usually anyone who lives in the neighbourhood can take part. Families with children are welcome too.
34152.m: People from the neighbourhood take part in the neighbourhood association.

34153.q: What does a neighbourhood association work for, for example?
34153.e: A neighbourhood association makes sure the neighbourhood is pleasant and safe. That includes safe routes for children.
34153.m: A neighbourhood association works for safe routes.

34154.q: What can a neighbourhood association let people sell on a square in the neighbourhood?
a: Old things at a flea market
34154.e: At a flea market people sell their old toys, books and clothes. Neighbourhood associations often organise this.
34154.m: At a flea market you sell old things.

34155.q: What are the people who live next door called?
34155.e: Neighbours live in the same building or right next door. A neighbourhood association brings neighbours together.
34155.m: A neighbourhood association brings neighbours together.

34156.q: Which two cantons are completely surrounded by the canton of St Gallen?
34156.e: The two Appenzell cantons lie in the middle of the canton of St Gallen. All around, they border only on St Gallen.
34156.m: The two Appenzells are completely surrounded by St Gallen.

34157.q: Which canton lies furthest west in Switzerland?
34157.e: The westernmost point of Switzerland is near Chancy in the canton of Geneva. There the Rhône flows into France.
34157.m: Geneva is the westernmost canton of Switzerland.

34158.q: In which canton is the centre point of Switzerland?
34158.e: The geographical centre of Switzerland is the Älggi Alp. It is in the municipality of Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden.
34158.m: The centre point of Switzerland is in Obwalden.

34159.q: Which canton lies furthest north in Switzerland?
34159.e: The northernmost point of Switzerland is near Bargen in the canton of Schaffhausen. The canton lies north of the Rhine.

34160.q: Which canton lies furthest south in Switzerland?
34160.e: The southernmost point of Switzerland is near Chiasso in Ticino. The canton lies south of the Alps.

34161.q: What is the most important law of a canton called?
34161.e: Every canton has its own constitution. It contains the most important rules for the canton.
34161.m: Every canton has its own cantonal constitution.

34162.q: Which canton lies furthest east in Switzerland?
34162.e: The easternmost point of Switzerland is in the Val Müstair in the Grisons. There you are already very close to Italy.
34162.m: The Grisons is the easternmost canton.

34163.q: Which canton is the smallest in Switzerland?
34163.e: Basel-Stadt is only about 37 square kilometres in size. The canton is made up only of the city of Basel and the municipalities of Riehen and Bettingen.

34164.q: What do you call the most important town of a canton?
34164.e: Every canton has a capital. The cantonal government and parliament work there.

34165.q: What usually has its seat in the capital of a canton?
34165.e: A canton's government works in the capital. That is why the capital is important for the whole canton.
34165.m: The cantonal government sits in the capital.

34166.q: What is the capital of the canton of Thurgau?
34166.e: The capital of Thurgau is Frauenfeld. The cantonal government meets there.
34166.m: Frauenfeld is the capital of Thurgau.

34167.q: Is the capital always the biggest town in the canton?
34167.e: In the canton of Basel-Landschaft, for example, Allschwil is bigger than the capital. The capital is the seat of government, not necessarily the biggest town.
34167.m: The capital is not always the biggest town.

34168.q: Which canton has a capital with the same name?
34168.e: The capital of the canton of Lucerne is also called Lucerne. This is the case in several cantons.
34168.m: The capital of Lucerne is also called Lucerne.

34169.q: What is the capital of the canton of Basel-Stadt?
34169.e: Basel is the capital and the biggest municipality of Basel-Stadt. The city lies on the Rhine.
34169.m: Basel is the capital of Basel-Stadt.

34170.q: What is the capital of the canton of Zurich?
34170.e: Zurich is the capital of the canton of Zurich. It is also the biggest city in Switzerland.
34170.m: Zurich is the capital of the canton of Zurich.

34171.q: What is the capital of the canton of Fribourg?
34171.e: The capital has the same name as the canton of Fribourg. Its old town is one of the largest medieval old towns in Switzerland.
34171.m: Fribourg is the capital of the canton of Fribourg.

34172.q: How many stars does the coat of arms of the canton of Valais have?
34172.e: The Valais coat of arms is white and red and has 13 stars. They stand for the 13 old districts, which were called Zenden.
34172.m: The Valais coat of arms has 13 stars.

34173.q: What can you see on the coat of arms of the canton of Aargau?
34173.e: On the left, the Aargau coat of arms shows white waves on black. They stand for the River Aare. On the right there are three white stars on blue.
34173.m: The Aargau coat of arms shows waves and three stars.

34174.q: Which flag often hangs next to the Swiss flag on 1 August?
34174.e: On the national holiday many people also hang out the flag of their canton. That shows where they come from.
34174.m: On 1 August the cantonal flag often hangs out too.

34175.q: What were coats of arms mainly used for in the past?
34175.e: Knights in armour looked very similar. You could recognise them by the picture on their shield.
34175.m: In the past knights were recognised by their coat of arms.

34176.q: What can you see on the coat of arms of the canton of St Gallen?
a: A bundle of rods with an axe
34176.e: The St Gallen coat of arms is green with a white bundle of rods and an axe. It stands for the unity of the canton.
34176.m: The St Gallen coat of arms shows a bundle of rods.

34177.q: What separates two cantons from each other?
34177.e: There is a cantonal border between two cantons. You can cross it without a passport.
34177.m: There is a cantonal border between cantons.

34178.q: Do you need a passport to travel to another canton?
34178.e: All cantons belong to Switzerland. So you can travel freely from one canton to another.
34178.m: You do not need a passport between cantons.

34179.q: What are borders often marked with out in the countryside?
34179.e: Boundary stones show exactly where a border runs. Coats of arms or letters are often carved into them.
34179.m: Boundary stones mark borders in the countryside.

34180.q: How many other cantons does the canton of Geneva border on?
34180.e: Geneva borders only on the canton of Vaud. Otherwise Geneva is almost completely surrounded by France.
34180.m: Geneva borders on only one Swiss canton.

34181.e: The canton of Ticino has a long border with Italy. People there speak Italian too.

34182.e: The Grisons borders on the Austrian states of Vorarlberg and Tyrol. St Gallen also borders on Austria.

34183.q: Which lake borders on the cantons of Zurich, Schwyz and St Gallen?
34183.e: Lake Zurich lies in three cantons. The cantonal borders run right through the water.
34183.m: Lake Zurich borders on Zurich, Schwyz and St Gallen.

34184.q: How can you often tell there is a cantonal border on the road?
a: By a sign with the canton's name
34184.e: On many roads there is a sign at the cantonal border. It shows the name of the canton and often its coat of arms.
34184.m: There is often a sign at the cantonal border.

34185.e: The cantonal council is made up of people's representatives. They discuss the canton's laws.
34185.m: The cantonal council is the parliament of the canton.

34186.q: Who elects the members of the cantonal council?
34186.e: The canton's voters elect the cantonal council. This happens every four or five years.
34186.m: The people elect the cantonal council.

34187.q: What does the cantonal council mainly do?
34187.e: The cantonal council passes the canton's laws. It also decides what the canton spends money on.
34187.m: The cantonal council passes the canton's laws.

34188.q: What is the cantonal parliament called in the canton of Bern?
34188.e: In Bern the cantonal parliament is called the Grand Council. Basel-Stadt and Aargau also call it that.
34188.m: In Bern the parliament is called the Grand Council.

34189.q: How many members does the Zurich cantonal council have?
34189.e: The Zurich cantonal council has 180 members. That makes it the biggest cantonal parliament in Switzerland.
34189.m: The Zurich cantonal council has 180 members.

34190.q: What is the cantonal parliament called in Uri?
34190.e: In Uri the cantonal parliament is called the Landrat. This name is also used in Glarus, Nidwalden and Basel-Landschaft.
34190.m: In Uri the parliament is called the Landrat.

34191.q: Where does a cantonal parliament usually meet?
34191.e: The sessions are usually held in the town hall. There is a large chamber there for the members.
34191.m: The cantonal parliament usually meets in the town hall.

34192.q: What is the cantonal parliament of Vaud called in French?
34192.e: In Vaud the parliament is called the Grand Conseil. That means “Grand Council”.
34192.m: The Vaud parliament is called the Grand Conseil.

34193.q: Who elects the government in the cantons?
34193.e: In all cantons the people elect the government directly. That is different from the Federal Council.
34193.m: The people elect the cantonal government.

34194.q: How many members does the government of the canton of Zurich have?
34194.e: The Zurich government has seven members. Each member heads a department.
34194.m: The Zurich government has seven members.

34195.q: What is the cantonal government of Geneva called in French?
34195.e: In French-speaking Switzerland the government is called the Conseil d'État. In English that means Council of State.
34195.m: In Geneva the government is called the Conseil d'État.

34196.q: How often does the president of the cantonal government usually change?
34196.e: The chair of the cantonal government usually changes every year. That way every member gets a turn.
34196.m: The president of the cantonal government usually changes every year.

34197.q: What does a member of the cantonal government head?
34197.e: Each member is responsible for one area, for example education or health. This area is called a directorate or department.
34197.m: Each member of the government heads a department.

34198.q: What is the government called in the canton of Bern?
34198.e: The government of the canton of Bern is called the Regierungsrat, the Executive Council. The Grand Council is the canton's parliament.
34198.m: The Bern government is called the Regierungsrat.

34199.q: Where is the government elected in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
34199.e: In Appenzell Innerrhoden the voters gather outdoors at the Landsgemeinde, an open-air assembly. There they also elect the government.
34199.m: In Appenzell Innerrhoden the Landsgemeinde elects the government.

34200.q: How long does a term in the cantonal government usually last?
34200.e: In most cantons the government is elected every four years. In some cantons it is five years.
34200.m: A term in the cantonal government usually lasts four years.

34201.q: Where do police officers learn their job?
34201.e: Anyone who wants to join the police goes to a police academy. There you learn about laws, first aid and traffic rules, for example.
34201.m: Police officers learn their job at a police academy.

34202.q: What is the police emergency number in Switzerland?
34202.e: You reach the police by calling 117. The call is free.
34202.m: You can reach the police on 117.

34203.q: What is the cantonal police (Kantonspolizei) called for short in German-speaking Switzerland?
34203.e: Kapo is short for Kantonspolizei. The word is often written on police cars.
34203.m: The cantonal police are called Kapo for short.

34204.q: Which police force is there in the city of Zurich as well as the cantonal police?
34204.e: Some big cities like Zurich and Winterthur have their own city police. They work together with the cantonal police.
34204.m: Zurich also has a city police force.

34205.q: What do the cantonal police often check on the roads?
34205.e: The police measure how fast cars are going. Anyone driving too fast has to pay a fine.
34205.m: The police check the speed of cars.

34206.q: What are the cantonal police called in Italian in Ticino?
34206.e: People in Ticino speak Italian. That is why the cantonal police there are called Polizia cantonale.
34206.m: In Ticino the cantonal police are called Polizia cantonale.

34207.q: What are the cantonal police called in French in Vaud?
34207.e: People in Vaud speak French. There the cantonal police are called Police cantonale.
34207.m: In Vaud the cantonal police are called Police cantonale.

34208.q: Who often helps the police at road accidents?
a: The fire brigade and ambulance service
34208.e: At big accidents the fire brigade and the ambulance service come too. Together they help the injured.
34208.m: Police, fire brigade and ambulance service work together at accidents.

34209.e: In many cantons the Gymnasium, a kind of grammar school, is called a Kantonsschule. The canton runs this school.
34209.m: A Kantonsschule is often a Gymnasium.

34210.q: What do many pupils in German-speaking Switzerland call the Kantonsschule for short?
34210.e: “Kanti” is the short form of Kantonsschule. You often hear the word in German-speaking Switzerland.
34210.m: The Kantonsschule is called Kanti for short.

34211.q: Which qualification do you get at a Gymnasium?
34211.e: At the end of the Gymnasium there is the Matura exam. It is the final qualification of the Kantonsschule.
34211.m: At a Gymnasium you take the Matura.

34212.q: When is the earliest you can move to a Kantonsschule or Gymnasium?
34212.e: Depending on the canton, the Gymnasium starts after primary school or after secondary school. You usually need to pass an exam to get in.
34212.m: The earliest you can go to a Gymnasium is after primary school.

34213.q: What do you usually need to get into a Gymnasium?
34213.e: In many cantons you have to pass an entrance exam. Sometimes good marks are enough.
34213.m: You usually need an entrance exam for the Gymnasium.

34214.q: Who decides the school holidays in Switzerland?
34214.e: The school holidays are set by the cantons and municipalities. That is why the holidays are not the same everywhere.
34214.m: The school holidays are not the same in all cantons.

34215.q: What is the Gymnasium often called in French-speaking Switzerland?
34215.e: In Vaud the Gymnasium is called “gymnase”. It also leads to the Matura.
34215.m: In Vaud the Gymnasium is called gymnase.

34216.q: Where can you go to study after the Matura?
34216.e: With the Matura you can study at a university. There you can learn medicine or law, for example.
34216.m: With the Matura you can go to university.

a: A railway station of the canton
34217.e: A cantonal hospital is a large hospital. It belongs to the canton or is supported by it.
34217.m: A cantonal hospital is a large hospital in the canton.

34218.q: Which number do you call for an ambulance?
34218.e: The number 144 calls the ambulance service. It takes injured people to hospital.
34218.m: You can reach the ambulance service on 144.

34219.q: Who works in a hospital and cares for sick people?
34219.e: Nurses look after the patients. They work closely with the doctors.
34219.m: Nurses care for sick people in hospital.

34220.q: Where do you go first in a hospital in an emergency?
34220.e: In an emergency you go to the emergency department. There sick and injured people get help straight away.
34220.m: In an emergency you go to the emergency department.

34221.q: What are seriously injured people sometimes flown to hospital in?
34221.e: Rescue helicopters fly quickly to accidents. In Switzerland this is done by Rega, for example.
34221.m: Rescue helicopters fly seriously injured people to hospital.

34222.q: In which town is the cantonal hospital of Aargau?
34222.e: The Aarau cantonal hospital is the biggest hospital in Aargau. There is another one in Baden.
34222.m: The Aargau cantonal hospital is in Aarau.

34223.q: What is a hospital called where doctors are also trained?
34223.e: At a university hospital students learn to be doctors. There are such hospitals in Zurich and Basel, for example.
34223.m: Doctors are also trained at a university hospital.

34224.q: Who mainly looks after the hospitals in Switzerland?
34224.e: Healthcare is mainly the job of the cantons. They plan which hospitals are needed.
34224.m: The cantons look after the hospitals.

34225.q: What do the two letters on a Swiss number plate show?
34225.e: The two letters show which canton the car is registered in. A number follows.
34225.m: The letters on the number plate show the canton.

34226.q: Which letters do cars from the Grisons have on their number plates?
34226.e: The Grisons has the letters GR. They are the first letters of its German name “Graubünden”.
34226.m: Cars from the Grisons have GR on their number plates.

34227.q: Which letters do cars from Ticino have on their number plates?
34227.e: The letters TI come from the Italian name of the canton, Ticino. People in Ticino speak Italian.
34227.m: Cars from Ticino have TI on their number plates.

34228.q: Which letters do cars from Valais have on their number plates?
34228.e: Valais is called Vallesia in Latin and Valais in French. The letters are VS.
34228.m: Cars from Valais have VS on their number plates.

34229.q: What can you see on the rear number plate next to the number?
a: A picture of the Federal Palace
34229.e: The rear plate shows the Swiss coat of arms and the cantonal coat of arms. So you can recognise the canton from the picture too.
34229.m: The rear number plate shows the cantonal coat of arms.

34230.q: Which letters do cars from Fribourg have on their number plates?
34230.e: The letters FR come from the French name of the canton. In Fribourg people speak French and German.
34230.m: Cars from Fribourg have FR on their number plates.

34231.q: Which letters do cars from Zurich have on their number plates?
34231.e: The canton of Zurich has the letters ZH. It is one of the most common plates in Switzerland.
34231.m: Cars from Zurich have ZH on their number plates.

34232.q: Which letters do cars from Nidwalden have on their number plates?
34232.e: Nidwalden has the letters NW. The N and the W stand for Nid and Walden.
34232.m: Cars from Nidwalden have NW on their number plates.

34233.q: What colour is the writing on a normal Swiss number plate?
34233.e: Normal number plates are white with black writing. That makes them easy to read.
34233.m: A number plate has black writing on a white background.

34234.q: Which language is the official language in most cantons?
34234.e: German is the official language in most cantons. Most people in Switzerland speak German.
34234.m: German is the official language in most cantons.

34235.q: How many cantons have only French as their official language?
34235.e: Four cantons in western Switzerland have only French as their official language, for example Geneva and Vaud.
34235.m: Four cantons have only French as their official language.

34236.q: Which language do people speak in the canton of Uri?
34236.e: Uri is in Central Switzerland. Its official language is German.

34237.q: What is the city of Geneva called in French?
34237.e: People in Geneva speak French. In French it is written Genève, with an accent on the second e.
34237.m: Geneva is called Genève in French.

34238.q: How many cantons have exactly two official languages?
34238.e: Three cantons, for example Fribourg and Valais, have German and French as official languages. The Grisons even has three.
34238.m: Three cantons have exactly two official languages.

34239.q: What is the canton of the Grisons called in Romansh?
34239.e: In Romansh the canton is called Grischun. Grigioni is the Italian name, Grisons the French one and Graubünden the German one.
34239.m: The Grisons is called Grischun in Romansh.

34240.q: What is the canton of Neuchâtel called in French?
34240.e: In French the canton is called Neuchâtel. That means “new castle”. In German it is called Neuenburg.
34240.m: The canton is called Neuchâtel in French.

34241.q: What is the canton of Fribourg called in French?
34241.e: In French the canton is called Fribourg, written with “ou”. In German it is called Freiburg.
34241.m: The canton is called Fribourg in French.

34242.q: What is the canton of Vaud called in French?
34242.e: In French the canton is called Vaud. In German it is called Waadt. Its capital is Lausanne.
34242.m: The canton is called Vaud in French.

34243.q: Who sets most public holidays in Switzerland?
34243.e: The cantons decide most public holidays themselves. That is why people do not have the same days off everywhere.
34243.m: The cantons set most public holidays.

34244.q: On which date is St Berchtold's Day?
34244.e: St Berchtold's Day is the day after New Year's Day. It is a day off in many cantons.
34244.m: St Berchtold's Day is on 2 January.

34245.q: Which canton celebrates the Näfelser Fahrt?
34245.e: The Näfelser Fahrt remembers the Battle of Näfels in 1388. It takes place in April.

34246.q: Which canton has a public holiday every year on 1 March?
34246.e: On 1 March 1848 Neuchâtel became a republic. The holiday remembers this.
34246.m: Neuchâtel celebrates its republic on 1 March.

34247.q: Which canton celebrates its independence on 23 June?
34247.e: On 23 June 1974 the people of the northern Jura voted for a canton of their own. This holiday remembers that.

34248.e: The Jeûne genevois is a Geneva public holiday in September. The name means “Geneva Fast”.

34249.q: On which date is St Stephen's Day?
34249.e: St Stephen's Day is the day after Christmas. It is a public holiday in many cantons.
34249.m: St Stephen's Day is on 26 December.

34250.q: Which holiday on 15 August is a day off mainly in Catholic cantons?
34250.e: Assumption Day is a Catholic holiday. In cantons like Lucerne or Ticino it is a day off.

34251.q: Which public holiday is always on a Thursday?
34251.e: Ascension Day is 39 days after Easter Sunday, so it is always on a Thursday. It is a day off in all cantons.
34251.m: Ascension Day is always on a Thursday.

34252.q: Which railway station is the biggest in Switzerland?
34252.e: About 3,000 trains arrive at and leave Zurich main station every day. No other Swiss station is as big.
34252.m: Zurich main station is the biggest railway station in Switzerland.

34253.q: Which hall at Zurich Zoo shows a rainforest from Madagascar?
34253.e: Real rainforest plants grow in the Masoala Hall. Animals from Madagascar, such as lemurs, live there too.
34253.m: The Masoala Hall at Zurich Zoo is a rainforest.

34254.q: Which river flows right through the city of Zurich?
34254.e: The Limmat comes out of Lake Zurich and flows through Zurich's old town. Later it flows into the Aare.
34254.m: The Limmat flows through the city of Zurich.

34255.q: What is burned at the Sechseläuten festival in Zurich?
34255.e: The Böögg is a snowman made of cotton wool and fireworks. If its head explodes quickly, the summer is supposed to be good.
34255.m: At Zurich's Sechseläuten the Böögg burns.

34256.q: Which town is the second biggest in the canton of Zurich?
34256.e: Winterthur has over 110,000 inhabitants. After Zurich it is the biggest town in the canton.
34256.m: Winterthur is the second biggest town in the canton of Zurich.

34257.q: What is the name of Zurich's local mountain?
34257.e: The Uetliberg is right next to the city of Zurich. From the top you can see over the city and the lake to the Alps.
34257.m: The Uetliberg is Zurich's local mountain.

34258.q: On which big lake is the city of Zurich?
34258.e: The city of Zurich lies at the lower end of Lake Zurich. The lake is about 40 kilometres long.
34258.m: The city of Zurich lies on Lake Zurich.

34259.q: Which caves on Lake Thun are named after a saint who is said to have driven a dragon out of them?
34259.e: According to legend, Saint Beatus drove a dragon out of the cave and then lived in it himself. Today you can visit the caves with their stalactites.
34259.m: The St Beatus Caves are on Lake Thun.

34260.q: Which canton is the second biggest in Switzerland by area?
34260.e: Only the Grisons is bigger than the canton of Bern. Bern stretches from the Jura to the high Alps.
34260.m: Bern is the second biggest canton in Switzerland.

34261.q: Which deep gorge near Meiringen can you walk through on walkways?
34261.e: The Aare Gorge is about 1.4 kilometres long and in places only a few metres wide. You walk along walkways on the rock walls.
34261.m: Near Meiringen you can walk through the Aare Gorge.

34262.q: What is the Bernese dish with lots of meat, sausages, sauerkraut and beans called?
34262.e: The Bernese Platter is a big feast. It is served with bacon, sausages, beef, sauerkraut and beans.
34262.m: The Bernese Platter is a dish with lots of meat.

34263.q: Which part of the canton of Bern do the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau belong to?
34263.e: The Bernese Oberland is the mountainous south of the canton of Bern. The three famous mountains stand there.
34263.m: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau are in the Bernese Oberland.

34264.q: Between which two lakes is Interlaken?
34264.e: The name Interlaken means “between the lakes”. The town lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.
34264.m: Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.

34265.q: Which cheese with big holes is named after a region of Bern?
34265.e: Emmentaler originally comes from the Emmental in the canton of Bern. It is famous for its big holes.
34265.m: Emmentaler with its big holes comes from the Emmental.

34266.q: Which valley in the Bernese Oberland is famous for its many waterfalls?
34266.e: It is also called the “valley of 72 waterfalls”. The Staubbach Falls are among the best known.
34266.m: The Lauterbrunnen Valley has very many waterfalls.

34267.q: What is the old wooden bridge with a water tower in Lucerne called?
34267.e: The Chapel Bridge is a covered wooden bridge in the middle of the town. Next to it stands the eight-sided water tower.
34267.m: The Chapel Bridge is the landmark of Lucerne.

34268.q: Up which mountain near Lucerne does the world's steepest cogwheel railway run?
34268.e: The Pilatus railway has a gradient of up to 48 per cent. It is considered the steepest cogwheel railway in the world.
34268.m: The world's steepest cogwheel railway goes up Pilatus.

34269.q: Which animal is shown on the famous monument carved into a rock in Lucerne?
34269.e: The Lion Monument shows a dying lion. It remembers Swiss soldiers who died in Paris in 1792.
34269.m: The Lion Monument in Lucerne shows a dying lion.

34270.q: Which big museum about trains, cars, ships and aeroplanes is in Lucerne?
34270.e: At the Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne you can see locomotives, aeroplanes and much more. It is one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.
34270.m: The Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne is all about transport.

34271.q: Which festival with lots of Guggenmusik bands is especially famous in Lucerne?
34271.e: Lucerne Carnival is one of the biggest in Switzerland. Lots of Guggenmusik bands play loudly in the streets.

34272.q: Which clock in Lucerne is allowed to strike one minute before all the other clocks in the town?
a: The clock on the Zyt Tower of the Musegg Wall
The clock at the railway station
The clock on the Chapel Bridge
The clock on the town hall
34272.e: The Musegg Wall is an old town wall with towers. The clock on the Zyt Tower is the oldest in the town, so it is allowed to strike first.
34272.m: The clock on the Zyt Tower of the Musegg Wall strikes first in Lucerne.

34273.q: Which region in the canton of Lucerne is a UNESCO biosphere?
34273.e: The Entlebuch has moors, forests and mountains. It has been a UNESCO biosphere since 2001.
34273.m: The Entlebuch is a UNESCO biosphere.

34274.q: At which village in Uri does the Gotthard Base Tunnel begin in the north?
34274.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is 57 kilometres long. Its northern entrance is near Erstfeld in the canton of Uri.
34274.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel begins at Erstfeld.

34275.q: Whose monument stands on the village square in Altdorf?
34275.e: The Tell Monument shows William Tell with his son. According to legend, Tell shot the apple off his son's head in Altdorf.
34275.m: The monument to William Tell stands in Altdorf.

34276.q: What is the southernmost part of Lake Lucerne called?
34276.e: Lake Uri stretches from Flüelen to Brunnen. It is surrounded by steep mountains.
34276.m: The southernmost part of Lake Lucerne is called Lake Uri.

34277.q: Which pass links the canton of Uri with the Bernese Oberland?
34277.e: The Susten Pass goes from Wassen in Uri to Innertkirchen in the canton of Bern. At the top you can see the Stein Glacier.
34277.m: The Susten Pass links Uri and Bern.

34278.q: What is the famous bridge in the Schöllenen Gorge called?
34278.e: The Devil's Bridge crosses the river in the Schöllenen Gorge near Andermatt. A legend says the devil built the first bridge.
34278.m: The Devil's Bridge is in the Schöllenen Gorge.

34279.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Uri?
34279.e: The Uri coat of arms is yellow with a black bull's head. The bull has a red ring in its nose.
34279.m: The Uri coat of arms shows a bull's head.

34280.q: Which river flows through the Reuss valley in Uri?
34280.e: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area. It flows through the whole of Uri into Lake Lucerne.

34281.q: Which pass links the canton of Uri with the canton of Glarus?
34281.e: The Klausen Pass goes from Altdorf to Linthal in the canton of Glarus. In winter the pass road is closed.
34281.m: The Klausen Pass links Uri and Glarus.

34282.q: What is the huge cave in the Muota valley called?
34282.e: The Hölloch in the Muota valley is over 200 kilometres long. It is one of the longest caves in the world.
34282.m: The Hölloch in the Muota valley is one of the longest caves in the world.

34283.q: What do the weather prophets of the Muota valley (Wetterschmöcker) do?
34283.e: The weather prophets watch animals and plants. From this they forecast the weather for the coming months.
34283.m: The weather prophets in the Muota valley forecast the weather.

34284.q: Which mountain on Lake Lucerne is called the “Queen of the Mountains”?
34284.e: The summit of the Rigi, Rigi Kulm, is in the canton of Schwyz. A cogwheel railway was already running up it in 1871.
34284.m: The Rigi is called the “Queen of the Mountains”.

34285.q: Which famous monastery with a Black Madonna is in the canton of Schwyz?
34285.e: Einsiedeln Abbey is the most important place of pilgrimage in Switzerland. Many people visit the Black Madonna there.
34285.m: The Black Madonna is in Einsiedeln Abbey.

34286.q: Which pointed mountain towers above the town of Schwyz?
34286.e: The Grosser Mythen is almost 1,900 metres high. Because of its shape it is easy to spot from far away.
34286.m: The Grosser Mythen towers above Schwyz.

34287.q: Which world-famous tool is made in Ibach in the canton of Schwyz?
34287.e: Pocket knives have been made in Ibach near Schwyz for over 100 years. The red knife with the cross is known all over the world.
34287.m: The Swiss Army knife comes from Ibach in the canton of Schwyz.

34288.q: Which lake near Einsiedeln is the biggest reservoir in Switzerland?
34288.e: Lake Sihl was dammed in 1937. It has the largest surface area of all the reservoirs in Switzerland.
34288.m: Lake Sihl is the biggest reservoir in Switzerland.

34289.q: Which lake is next to the village of Lungern in Obwalden?
34289.e: Lake Lungern is in the south of Obwalden. It is used for a hydroelectric power station.
34289.m: Lake Lungern is near Lungern in Obwalden.

34290.q: Which lake is next to the capital of Obwalden?
34290.e: Lake Sarnen lies in the middle of Obwalden. It is named after the town of Sarnen.

34291.q: Which canton does the holiday resort of Engelberg belong to?
34291.e: Engelberg belongs to the canton of Obwalden but is separated from the rest of the canton. You travel through Nidwalden to get there.

34292.q: Which glacier mountain near Engelberg has a cable car that rotates during the ride?
34292.e: The rotating cable car up the Titlis is called the Rotair. During the ride it turns all the way round once.
34292.m: A rotating cable car goes up the Titlis.

34293.q: Which saint from Obwalden is considered the patron saint of Switzerland?
34293.e: Niklaus von Flüe lived in the 15th century in the Ranft near Flüeli. He is called Brother Klaus.
34293.m: Brother Klaus from Obwalden is the patron saint of Switzerland.

34294.q: Which object can be seen on the coats of arms of both Obwalden and Nidwalden?
34294.e: Both coats of arms show a double key. It is the symbol of Saint Peter.
34294.m: The coats of arms of Obwalden and Nidwalden show a key.

34295.q: Which pass links Obwalden with the Bernese Oberland?
34295.e: The Brünig Pass goes from Lungern in Obwalden to Brienzwiler in the canton of Bern. It is only just over 1,000 metres high.
34295.m: The Brünig Pass takes you from Obwalden to the Bernese Oberland.

34296.q: What is made at the Glasi in Hergiswil in the canton of Nidwalden?
34296.e: At the Glasi Hergiswil glass is blown by hand. Visitors can watch.
34296.m: At the Glasi Hergiswil glass is blown.

34297.q: What were Obwalden and Nidwalden called together in the past?
34297.e: Together Obwalden and Nidwalden formed old Unterwalden. Today they are two separate cantons.
34297.m: Together Obwalden and Nidwalden were called Unterwalden.

34298.q: Up which mountain does a cable car with an open upper deck run?
34298.e: The CabriO cable car has run up the Stanserhorn since 2012. You can ride on its roof under the open sky.
34298.m: A cable car with an open roof goes up the Stanserhorn.

34299.q: Which hero from Nidwalden has a monument in Stans?
34299.e: According to legend, Arnold Winkelried helped the Confederates win the Battle of Sempach in 1386. A monument in Stans remembers him.
34299.m: The monument to Arnold Winkelried stands in Stans.

34300.q: Which ski area lies above Beckenried in the canton of Nidwalden?
34300.e: The Klewenalp lies high above Lake Lucerne. A cable car goes up from Beckenried.

34301.q: What is built in a big factory in Stans?
34301.e: Aeroplanes have been built in Stans for many decades. Buochs airfield is right next to it.

34302.q: Which mountain with famous hotels lies mostly in the canton of Nidwalden?
34302.e: The Bürgenstock juts out into Lake Lucerne. At the top there are large hotels with wide views.
34302.m: The Bürgenstock is on Lake Lucerne in Nidwalden.

34303.q: What is the capital of the canton of Glarus?
34303.e: The capital of the canton of Glarus is also called Glarus. It lies at the foot of the Glärnisch.
34303.m: The capital of the canton of Glarus is Glarus.

34304.q: Which lake lies on the border between Glarus and St Gallen?
34304.e: Lake Walen lies between the cantons of Glarus and St Gallen. The steep Churfirsten mountains rise on its northern shore.
34304.m: Lake Walen lies between Glarus and St Gallen.

34305.q: Through which hole in the rock does the sun shine onto the church of Elm twice a year?
34305.e: The Martinsloch is a big hole in a rocky ridge above Elm. In spring and autumn the sun shines straight through it onto the church tower.
34305.m: The sun shines through the Martinsloch onto the church of Elm.

34306.q: Which green cheese comes from the canton of Glarus?
34306.e: Glarus Schabziger is green because it contains herbs. People grate it over pasta, for example.

34307.q: Which lake lies in a valley west of the town of Glarus?
34307.e: Lake Klöntal lies in the Klöntal valley below the Glärnisch. It is a popular place for days out.
34307.m: Lake Klöntal is in the canton of Glarus.

34308.q: Which is the highest mountain in the canton of Glarus?
34308.e: The Tödi is 3,614 metres high. It lies on the border with the Grisons.
34308.m: The Tödi is the highest mountain in Glarus.

34309.q: Which holiday resort in the canton of Glarus is car-free?
34309.e: Braunwald lies on a sunny terrace above Linthal. You can only reach it by funicular.
34309.m: Braunwald is a car-free holiday resort.

34310.q: Which pastry filled with almonds and plums comes from the canton of Glarus?
34310.e: The Glarus pastry is made of puff pastry. Half of it is filled with almond paste and half with plum purée.
34310.m: The Glarus pastry is a sweet speciality from Glarus.

34311.q: Which sweet speciality is named after the canton of Zug?
34311.e: Zug cherry cake is soaked in kirsch, a cherry brandy. Lots of cherry trees grow in Zug.
34311.m: Zug cherry cake comes from Zug.

34312.q: On which lake is the town of Zug?
34312.e: The town of Zug lies on the north-east shore of Lake Zug. You can often see beautiful sunsets from there.
34312.m: The town of Zug lies on Lake Zug.

34313.q: What is the capital of the canton of Zug?
34313.e: The capital of the canton of Zug is also called Zug. Baar and Cham are other municipalities in the canton.
34313.m: The capital of the canton of Zug is Zug.

34314.q: What can you marvel at in the Höllgrotten caves near Baar?
34314.e: The Höllgrotten are caves with lots of stalactites and stalagmites. They lie in the Lorze gorge near Baar.
34314.m: The Höllgrotten near Baar have stalactites and stalagmites.

34315.q: By which lake in the canton of Zug did the Battle of Morgarten take place in 1315?
34315.e: According to tradition, the Battle of Morgarten took place by Lake Ägeri. The Confederates won the battle there.
34315.m: The Battle of Morgarten was by Lake Ägeri.

34316.q: What happened in the town of Zug in 1887?
a: The lake froze over for ever
34316.e: On 5 July 1887 part of the suburb slid into Lake Zug. Many houses sank, and people died.
34316.m: In 1887 part of Zug's suburb sank into the lake.

34317.q: What kind of railway goes up the Zugerberg?
34317.e: The Zugerberg railway is a funicular. It runs from Schönegg up to the Zugerberg.
34317.m: A funicular goes up the Zugerberg.

34318.q: Apart from the time, what does the special clock on the Zyt Tower in Zug show?
34318.e: Below the big clock face there is an astronomical clock. It shows the day of the week, the month and the phase of the moon.
34318.m: The clock on Zug's Zyt Tower also shows the phase of the moon.

34319.q: What powers the old funicular in the town of Fribourg?
34319.e: The cars have a tank that is filled with waste water at the top. The heavy car goes down and pulls the other one up.
34319.m: The funicular in Fribourg runs on waste water.

34320.q: What is the well-known mountain lake in the Sense district of the canton of Fribourg called?
34320.e: The Schwarzsee lies at just over 1,000 metres in the German-speaking part of the canton of Fribourg. In summer lots of people swim there, in winter people go skiing.
34320.m: The Schwarzsee is in the canton of Fribourg.

34321.q: Which cheese is named after a region in the canton of Fribourg?
34321.e: Gruyère is called Greyerzer in German. It comes from the Gruyère region with the little town of Gruyères.
34321.m: Gruyère cheese comes from the canton of Fribourg.

34322.q: Which little town with an old town wall lies on Lake Murten?
34322.e: Murten has a well-preserved ring wall that you can walk along. A famous battle took place there in 1476.
34322.m: Murten with its town wall lies on Lake Murten.

34323.q: Which 2,002-metre mountain is a landmark of the Gruyère region?
34323.e: The Moléson rises above the little town of Gruyères. From its summit you can see as far as Lake Geneva.
34323.m: The Moléson is the local mountain of the Gruyère region.

34324.q: Which river flows through the town of Fribourg?
34324.e: The Saane is called the Sarine in French. It flows through the town of Fribourg in a deep gorge.

34325.q: What is the Fribourg fondue made from two kinds of cheese called?
34325.e: “Moitié-moitié” means “half and half”. The fondue is half Gruyère and half Vacherin fribourgeois.
34325.m: The Fribourg fondue is called moitié-moitié.

34326.q: What is the main church of the town of Fribourg called?
34326.e: St Nicholas Cathedral has a tower 74 metres high. It stands in the middle of Fribourg's old town.
34326.m: St Nicholas Cathedral is in Fribourg.

34327.q: Which number is considered a special lucky number in the town of Solothurn?
34327.e: In Solothurn there are eleven of many things, for example fountains, churches and towers. So 11 is the town's number.

34328.q: What is the big cathedral in the town of Solothurn called?
34328.e: The cathedral is dedicated to Saint Ursus. It is a magnificent church from the 18th century.
34328.m: Solothurn's cathedral is called St Ursus.

34329.q: Who lives in the little house in the Verena Gorge near Solothurn?
34329.e: In the Verena Gorge there is a small chapel and a hermitage. For centuries a hermit, someone who lives alone and quietly, has lived there again and again.
34329.m: A hermit lives in the Verena Gorge.

34330.q: What is the name of Solothurn's local mountain in the Jura?
34330.e: The Weissenstein lies north of the town of Solothurn. A gondola goes up it.
34330.m: The Weissenstein is Solothurn's local mountain.

34331.q: What is the town of Grenchen in the canton of Solothurn known for?
34331.e: There have been lots of watch factories in Grenchen for over 150 years. That is why Grenchen is also called a watch town.

34332.q: Which town in the canton of Solothurn is an important railway junction?
34332.e: In Olten the railway lines from Zurich, Bern, Basel and Lucerne meet. That is why lots of people change trains there.
34332.m: Olten is an important railway junction.

34333.q: What is the town of Solothurn called during carnival?
34333.e: During carnival Solothurn becomes “Honolulu”. The name has been part of Solothurn's carnival for a long time.
34333.m: At carnival Solothurn is called Honolulu.

34334.q: Which fountain in Basel has figures that move and squirt water?
34334.e: The artist Jean Tinguely built this fountain with machine figures in 1977. They turn round and squirt water.
34334.m: Funny machines move in the Tinguely Fountain.

34335.q: How do the little ferries in Basel cross the Rhine?
a: Using the force of the current
34335.e: The Basel ferries hang from a cable over the Rhine. The river's current pushes them to the other bank without an engine.
34335.m: The Basel ferries are driven by the force of the Rhine.

34336.q: At what time does Basel carnival begin with the Morgestraich?
34336.e: On the Monday after Ash Wednesday all the lights in the city go out at 4 o'clock. Then the carnival groups set off with lanterns.
34336.m: The Morgestraich begins at 4 in the morning.

34337.q: Which hard biscuit with honey is a Basel speciality?
34337.e: Basler Läckerli are gingerbread biscuits with honey, nuts and candied fruit. They are known all over the world.

34338.q: What do the people of Basel call their zoo?
34338.e: Basel Zoo is the oldest zoo in Switzerland. The people of Basel fondly call it “Zolli”.
34338.m: Basel Zoo is called the Zolli.

34339.q: What do many people take with them when swimming in the Rhine in Basel so their clothes stay dry?
34339.e: The Wickelfisch is a waterproof bag shaped like a fish. You pack your clothes in it and swim down the Rhine with it.
34339.m: When swimming in the Rhine, clothes go in the Wickelfisch.

34340.q: Which two countries does the canton of Basel-Stadt border on?
34340.e: Basel lies where three countries meet. Switzerland, Germany and France come together here.
34340.m: Basel borders on Germany and France.

34341.q: What stone is Basel Minster built from?
34341.e: Basel Minster is built of red sandstone. That is why it glows reddish above the Rhine.
34341.m: Basel Minster is made of red sandstone.

34342.q: Which valley moved from the canton of Bern to the canton of Basel-Landschaft in 1994?
34342.e: The people of the Laufental voted for the change. Since 1994 the Laufental has belonged to the canton of Basel-Landschaft.
34342.m: The Laufental has belonged to Basel-Landschaft since 1994.

34343.q: What else is the canton of Basel-Landschaft called?
34343.e: People there often call their canton “Baselbiet”. The song “Baselbieter Lied” is even the cantonal anthem.
34343.m: The canton of Basel-Landschaft is also called Baselbiet.

34344.q: What do people carry in the Chienbäse parade in Liestal?
34344.e: On carnival Sunday people carry burning bundles of wood through the old town of Liestal. Burning carts also roll through the town gate.
34344.m: At the Chienbäse in Liestal big bundles of wood burn.

34345.q: What colour is the Basel crozier on the coat of arms of Basel-Landschaft?
34345.e: The coat of arms of Basel-Landschaft shows a red Basel crozier, a bishop's staff, on a white background. It recalls the Bishop of Basel.
34345.m: The Basel crozier on the coat of arms of Basel-Landschaft is red.

34346.q: Since which year has the canton of Basel-Landschaft existed?
34346.e: After a quarrel with the city of Basel, the countryside split off in 1833. That is how two half-cantons came about.
34346.m: Basel-Landschaft has been a canton of its own since 1833.

34347.q: In which place in the canton of Basel-Landschaft is the Roman town of Augusta Raurica?
34347.e: Augusta Raurica was a Roman town. Its remains are mainly in Augst and partly in Kaiseraugst in Aargau.

34348.q: Which fruit is the canton of Basel-Landschaft especially known for?
34348.e: There are very many cherry trees in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. In spring they blossom white, and in summer the cherries are picked.
34348.m: Basel-Landschaft is known for its cherries.

34349.q: What is the capital of the canton of Schaffhausen?
34349.e: The town of Schaffhausen is the capital of the canton of the same name. The government and parliament meet there.
34349.m: The capital of the canton of Schaffhausen is also called Schaffhausen.

34350.q: Which famous waterfall is in the canton of Schaffhausen?
34350.e: The Rhine Falls are at Neuhausen am Rheinfall, on the border with the canton of Zurich. They are among the biggest waterfalls in Europe.
34350.m: At the Rhine Falls the Rhine thunders down, loud and wide.

34351.q: What is the round fortress high above the town of Schaffhausen called?
34351.e: The Munot is a round fortress from the 16th century. It is the landmark of the town of Schaffhausen.
34351.m: The Munot is the round landmark of Schaffhausen.

34352.q: What rings every evening at 9 o'clock on the Munot?
34352.e: A tower keeper lives on the Munot. Every evening at 9 o'clock he rings the little Munot bell.
34352.m: Every evening at 9 o'clock the Munot bell rings.

34353.q: What is the abbreviation for the canton of Schaffhausen?
34353.e: Every canton has a two-letter abbreviation. For Schaffhausen it is SH, for example on number plates.

34354.q: Which neighbouring country almost completely surrounds the canton of Schaffhausen?
34354.e: The canton of Schaffhausen lies north of the Rhine. It is mostly surrounded by Germany.
34354.m: Schaffhausen is almost completely surrounded by Germany.

34355.q: Which little town in the canton of Schaffhausen is known for its painted houses?
34355.e: Stein am Rhein has a beautiful old town with brightly painted house fronts. Lots of tourists visit the little town.
34355.m: In Stein am Rhein many houses are brightly painted.

34356.q: Which language do people mainly speak in the canton of Schaffhausen?
34356.e: Schaffhausen is part of German-speaking Switzerland. In everyday life people there speak Swiss German.
34356.m: People speak German in the canton of Schaffhausen.

34357.q: Which place is the capital of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
34357.e: The government and parliament of Appenzell Ausserrhoden are in Herisau. It is the biggest village in the canton.
34357.m: Herisau is the capital of Appenzell Ausserrhoden.

34358.q: Which animal does the coat of arms of Appenzell Ausserrhoden show?
34358.e: The coat of arms shows an upright black bear. Next to it are the letters V and R for “Ussere Rhode”.
34358.m: The Ausserrhoden coat of arms shows a black bear.

34359.q: Which former canton did Appenzell Ausserrhoden come from?
34359.e: In 1597 the land of Appenzell split into two parts. That is how Ausserrhoden and Innerrhoden came about.
34359.m: Appenzell was split into two half-cantons in 1597.

34360.q: In which Ausserrhoden village do the Silvesterchläuse go round on New Year's Eve?
34360.e: In Urnäsch the Silvesterchläuse go from house to house with bells. This happens on 31 December and 13 January.
34360.m: In Urnäsch the Silvesterchläuse ring big bells.

34361.q: What is the abbreviation for the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
34361.e: The abbreviation AR stands for Appenzell Ausserrhoden. You can see it on number plates, for example.
34361.m: Appenzell Ausserrhoden has the abbreviation AR.

34362.q: In which Ausserrhoden village is the Pestalozzi Children's Village?
34362.e: The Pestalozzi Children's Village was founded in Trogen in 1946. Children who had lost their homes in the war lived there.
34362.m: The Pestalozzi Children's Village is in Trogen.

34363.q: Which faith was dominant in Ausserrhoden when Appenzell split in 1597?
34363.e: When the land split, the Protestants stayed in Ausserrhoden. The Catholics lived in Innerrhoden.
34363.m: Ausserrhoden was Protestant when the land split.

34364.q: What is the capital of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
34364.e: The village of Appenzell is the capital of Innerrhoden. It is known for its colourful houses.
34364.m: The capital of Innerrhoden is Appenzell.

34365.q: Which cave with a small chapel is near the Ebenalp?
34365.e: The Wildkirchli is made up of caves in a rock face. Hermits used to live there, and there is a small chapel.
34365.m: In the Wildkirchli near the Ebenalp there is a small cave chapel.

34366.q: Which sweet honey pastry is an Appenzell speciality?
34366.e: Appenzeller Biberli are gingerbread with honey and spices. Inside they have an almond filling.
34366.m: Appenzeller Biberli are filled honey gingerbreads.

34367.q: Which mountain is the highest in the Alpstein?
34367.e: The Säntis is about 2,502 metres high. You can ride a cable car to the summit.
34367.m: The Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein.

34368.q: Which mountain lake is in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
34368.e: The Seealpsee lies in the Alpstein below the Ebenalp. Lots of people hike there.
34368.m: The Seealpsee lies beautifully in the Alpstein.

34369.q: Which canton has the fewest inhabitants in Switzerland?
34369.e: Only about 16,000 people live in Appenzell Innerrhoden (as of 2024). No other canton has so few inhabitants.
34369.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden is the canton with the fewest inhabitants.

34370.q: What is the abbreviation for the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
34370.e: AI stands for Appenzell Innerrhoden. The abbreviation appears on number plates.
34370.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden has the abbreviation AI.

34371.q: What is the capital of the canton of St Gallen?
34371.e: The city of St Gallen is the capital of the canton. It is also the biggest town in the canton.
34371.m: The capital of the canton of St Gallen is the city of St Gallen.

34372.q: Who is the city of St Gallen named after?
34372.e: The monk Gallus lived in this place about 1,400 years ago. Later a monastery and the town grew up there.
34372.m: St Gallen is named after the monk Gallus.

34373.q: Which old library in St Gallen is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
34373.e: The Abbey Library belongs to the old monastery. It owns very old, handwritten books.
34373.m: The Abbey Library of St Gallen keeps ancient books.

34374.q: Which sausage is a well-known speciality from St Gallen?
34374.e: The St Gallen bratwurst is pale and made from veal and pork. Traditionally it is eaten without mustard.
34374.m: The St Gallen bratwurst is traditionally eaten without mustard.

34375.q: What is the big fair held every October in St Gallen called?
34375.e: The OLMA is a big fair for farming and food. It takes place every autumn in St Gallen.
34375.m: The OLMA takes place every autumn in St Gallen.

34376.q: Which handicraft once made St Gallen world-famous?
34376.e: St Gallen embroidery and lace were sold all over the world. Even today companies there make fine fabrics.
34376.m: St Gallen became famous for its embroidery.

34377.q: Which big lake does the canton of St Gallen border on in the north?
34377.e: The canton of St Gallen has a shore on Lake Constance near Rorschach. Thurgau also borders on this lake.
34377.m: The canton of St Gallen borders on Lake Constance.

34378.q: What is the abbreviation for the canton of St Gallen?
34378.e: SG stands for St Gallen. You can see the abbreviation on number plates.
34378.m: The canton of St Gallen has the abbreviation SG.

34379.q: In which place in the Grisons is the Spengler Cup ice hockey tournament held around New Year's Eve?
34379.e: The Spengler Cup is one of the oldest ice hockey tournaments in the world. It takes place every year between Christmas and New Year's Eve in Davos.
34379.m: The Spengler Cup is played every year in Davos.

34380.q: Which place in the Grisons has hosted the Winter Olympics twice?
34380.e: The Winter Olympics were held in St Moritz in 1928 and 1948. St Moritz is in the Upper Engadine.
34380.m: St Moritz has hosted the Winter Olympics twice.

34381.q: What is the highest mountain in the canton of the Grisons?
34381.e: Piz Bernina is about 4,049 metres high. It is the only four-thousand-metre peak in the Eastern Alps.
34381.m: Piz Bernina is the highest mountain in the Grisons.

34383.q: Where is Switzerland's only national park?
34383.e: The Swiss National Park is in the Engadine near Zernez. It was founded in 1914.
34383.m: Switzerland's only national park is in the Grisons.

34384.q: Which big river has its sources in the Grisons?
34384.e: The Anterior Rhine and the Posterior Rhine rise in the mountains of the Grisons. At Reichenau they flow together to form the Rhine.
34384.m: The Rhine has its sources in the Grisons.

34385.q: Which railway with red trains runs through the mountains of the Grisons?
34385.e: The Rhaetian Railway runs over many bridges and through tunnels. Some of its lines are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
34385.m: The Rhaetian Railway runs red trains through the Grisons.

34386.q: Which sweet speciality comes from the Engadine in the Grisons?
34386.e: The Grisons nut tart is filled with walnuts and caramel. It comes from the Engadine.
34386.m: The Grisons nut tart is filled with nuts and caramel.

34387.q: Which town in Aargau has a big castle on a hill in the middle of the town?
34387.e: Lenzburg Castle stands on a hill above the old town. Today it houses a museum.
34387.m: Lenzburg Castle sits on a hill above the town.

34388.q: What is the nickname of the canton of Aargau?
34388.e: Lots of carrots, called “Rüebli” in Swiss German, used to grow in Aargau. That is where the nickname “carrot land” comes from.

34389.q: Which famous ruling family has its ancestral castle in Aargau?
34389.e: Habsburg Castle is in the canton of Aargau. The family that later ruled Austria came from there.
34389.m: The Habsburgs originally came from Aargau.

34390.q: How many stars are on the coat of arms of the canton of Aargau?
34390.e: The Aargau coat of arms shows three white stars on a blue background. Next to them are waves for the rivers.
34390.m: Three white stars shine on the Aargau coat of arms.

34391.q: What is the place near Brugg called where the Aare, Reuss and Limmat flow together?
34391.e: Three big rivers meet near Brugg. This area is called the water castle of Switzerland.
34391.m: At the water castle the Aare, Reuss and Limmat flow together.

34392.q: Which town in Aargau is known for its warm thermal baths?
34392.e: Even the Romans bathed in the warm spring water in Baden. Today there is a modern thermal bath there.
34392.m: In Baden people have bathed in warm spring water since Roman times.

34393.q: What is the abbreviation for the canton of Aargau?
34393.e: AG stands for Aargau. You can see it on number plates from this canton.
34393.m: The canton of Aargau has the abbreviation AG.

34394.q: Which big river gives Aargau its name?
34394.e: The name Aargau means “area on the Aare”. The Aare flows right through the canton.
34394.m: Aargau is named after the River Aare.

34395.q: Which former monastery near Frauenfeld is now a place for days out with a museum?
34395.e: Monks used to live in Ittingen Charterhouse. Today it has gardens, museums and a hotel.
34395.m: Ittingen Charterhouse used to be a monastery.

34396.q: What nickname does Thurgau have because of its many apple trees?
34396.e: Very many apple trees grow in Thurgau. The apples are made into cider (Most), which is why it is called Mostindien, “Cider India”.
34396.m: Because of its many apples, Thurgau is also called Mostindien.

34397.q: Which river gives the canton of Thurgau its name?
34397.e: The Thur flows through the canton of Thurgau. The name means “area on the Thur”.
34397.m: Thurgau is named after the River Thur.

34398.q: From which place in Thurgau does a car ferry go to Germany?
34398.e: From Romanshorn the ferry crosses Lake Constance to Friedrichshafen. The crossing takes about 40 minutes.
34398.m: A ferry crosses Lake Constance from Romanshorn.

34399.q: Which lake does the canton of Thurgau border on?
34399.e: Thurgau has a long shore on Lake Constance. Towns like Arbon lie there.
34399.m: Thurgau has a long shore on Lake Constance.

34400.q: Which town in Thurgau lies right next to the German city of Konstanz?
34400.e: Kreuzlingen and Konstanz have grown together. The national border runs right between the two towns.
34400.m: Kreuzlingen borders directly on the German city of Konstanz.

34401.q: What is the abbreviation for the canton of Thurgau?
34401.e: TG stands for Thurgau. You can see the abbreviation on number plates.
34401.m: The canton of Thurgau has the abbreviation TG.

34402.q: Which very long railway tunnel ends in Ticino in the south?
34402.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is 57 kilometres long. It runs from Erstfeld in the canton of Uri to Bodio in Ticino.
34402.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel leads under the Alps to Ticino.

34403.q: Which river is the canton of Ticino named after?
34403.e: The River Ticino is called the Tessin in German. It flows through the canton into Lake Maggiore.
34403.m: The canton of Ticino is named after the River Ticino.

34404.q: What is Bellinzona especially known for?
34404.e: There are three medieval castles in Bellinzona. They have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.
34404.m: Bellinzona is known for its three old castles.

34405.q: Which is the biggest town in the canton of Ticino?
34405.e: Lugano has the most inhabitants in Ticino. The town lies on Lake Lugano.
34405.m: Lugano is the biggest town in Ticino.

34406.q: Which animal is the trophy at the Locarno Film Festival?
34406.e: At the Locarno Film Festival the best film wins the Golden Leopard. Films are also shown on the Piazza Grande.
34406.m: In Locarno the best film wins the Golden Leopard.

34407.q: On which mountain in Ticino were lots of fossilised sea creatures and reptiles found?
34407.e: On Monte San Giorgio lots of fossils were found from the time when there was a sea there. The mountain is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
34407.m: Lots of fossilised reptiles were found on Monte San Giorgio.

34408.q: Which big lake lies partly in Ticino and partly in Italy?
34408.e: Most of Lake Maggiore is in Italy. Its northern end with Locarno belongs to Ticino.
34408.m: Lake Maggiore lies partly in Ticino and partly in Italy.

34409.q: Why is Ticino called the “sun parlour” of Switzerland?
a: There are lots of solar panels there
34409.e: Ticino lies south of the Alps and has a mild climate. The sun shines often there, and even palm trees grow.
34409.m: Ticino is called the sun parlour because the sun often shines there.

34410.q: Which town in Vaud on Lake Geneva has a statue of Charlie Chaplin?
34410.e: Charlie Chaplin lived the last years of his life near Vevey. A statue on the lakeshore remembers him.
34410.m: A statue in Vevey remembers Charlie Chaplin.

34411.q: In which town in Vaud is the big Paléo open-air festival held?
34411.e: The Paléo Festival is one of the biggest open-air festivals in Switzerland. It takes place every summer in Nyon.
34411.m: The Paléo Festival takes place in Nyon.

34412.q: Which worldwide sports organisation has its headquarters in Lausanne?
34412.e: The International Olympic Committee organises the Olympic Games. Its headquarters are in Lausanne, which also has an Olympic Museum.
34412.m: The Olympic Committee has its headquarters in Lausanne.

34413.q: Which famous castle stands in the water of Lake Geneva near Montreux?
34413.e: Chillon Castle stands on a rock in the lake. It is one of the most visited castles in Switzerland.
34413.m: Chillon Castle stands on a rock in Lake Geneva.

34414.q: What are the steep slopes of Lavaux on Lake Geneva known for?
34414.e: In Lavaux vines grow on steep terraces above the lake. The area has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007.
34414.m: In Lavaux vines grow on steep terraces.

34415.q: What colours is the coat of arms of the canton of Vaud?
34415.e: The Vaud coat of arms is white at the top and green at the bottom. It bears the words “Liberté et Patrie”, which means freedom and fatherland.
34415.m: The Vaud coat of arms is white and green.

34416.q: Which big music festival takes place every summer in Montreux?
34416.e: The Montreux Jazz Festival has been held since 1967. Many famous musicians have performed there.
34416.m: A big jazz festival takes place in Montreux every summer.

34417.q: What are people from the canton of Vaud called in French?
34417.e: Someone from Vaud is called a Vaudois. In German they are called Waadtländer.
34417.m: People from Vaud are called Vaudois.

34418.q: Which big river flows through the whole of Valais?
34418.e: The Rhône rises at the Rhône Glacier in Valais. It flows through the whole valley into Lake Geneva.
34418.m: The Rhône flows through the whole of Valais.

34419.q: Which famous pointed mountain is in Valais?
34419.e: The Matterhorn is about 4,478 metres high. Because of its shape it is one of the best-known mountains in the world.
34419.m: The Matterhorn has a famous pointed shape.

34420.q: Which glacier, the biggest in the Alps, is in Valais?
34420.e: The Great Aletsch Glacier is about 20 kilometres long. It is the biggest glacier in the Alps.
34420.m: The Aletsch Glacier is the biggest glacier in the Alps.

34421.q: Which well-known mountain village in Valais is closed to cars?
34421.e: Only small electric vehicles drive in Zermatt. Visitors come to the village by train.
34421.m: Zermatt is a car-free mountain village.

34422.q: Which cows fight for the title of queen in the cow fights in Valais?
34422.e: Hérens cows are small, strong and mostly black. In the cow fights they push each other away with their heads.
34422.m: Hérens cows fight for the title of queen in Valais.

34423.q: Which mountain in Valais is the highest in Switzerland?
34423.e: The Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa area is 4,634 metres high. No mountain in Switzerland is higher.
34423.m: The Dufourspitze in Valais is the highest mountain in Switzerland.

34424.q: Which fruit grows especially often in Valais?
34424.e: Lots of apricots grow in the sunny valleys of Valais. Valais is the most important apricot region in Switzerland.
34424.m: Lots of apricots grow in Valais.

34425.q: Which cheese dish originally comes from Valais?
34425.e: For raclette, a wheel of cheese is heated and the soft cheese is scraped off. It is eaten with potatoes.
34425.m: Raclette is a cheese dish from Valais.

34426.q: What is the capital of the canton of Neuchâtel?
34426.e: The town of Neuchâtel is called Neuenburg in German. It is the capital of the canton.
34426.m: The town of Neuchâtel is the capital of the canton of Neuchâtel.

34427.q: Which is the biggest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland?
34427.e: Lake Neuchâtel lies completely in Switzerland. Lake Geneva and Lake Constance are bigger, but they lie partly in other countries.
34427.m: Lake Neuchâtel is the biggest lake entirely in Switzerland.

34428.q: What are La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle in the canton of Neuchâtel known for?
34428.e: Watches have been made in these towns for a long time. That is why they are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
34428.m: La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle are watch towns.

34429.q: Which language do people speak in the canton of Neuchâtel?
34429.e: Neuchâtel is in western Switzerland. People there speak French.
34429.m: People speak French in the canton of Neuchâtel.

34430.q: Which three colours does the coat of arms of the canton of Neuchâtel have?
34430.e: The Neuchâtel flag has three vertical stripes in green, white and red. At the top of the red stripe there is a small white cross.
34430.m: The Neuchâtel coat of arms is green, white and red.

34431.q: Which king also used to rule over Neuchâtel?
34431.e: Neuchâtel belonged to the King of Prussia for a long time. It only became a republic in 1848.
34431.m: Neuchâtel used to belong to the King of Prussia.

34432.q: Which huge rocky cirque is in the canton of Neuchâtel?
34432.e: The Creux du Van is a rocky cirque with cliffs up to 160 metres high. Ibex live there too.
34432.m: The Creux du Van is a huge rocky cirque in the Neuchâtel Jura.

34433.q: Which famous architect was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds?
34433.e: Le Corbusier was born in La Chaux-de-Fonds in 1887. He became one of the best-known architects in the world.
34433.m: Le Corbusier came from La Chaux-de-Fonds.

34434.q: What is the capital of the canton of Geneva?
34434.e: The city of Geneva is called Genève in French. It is the capital of the canton.
34434.m: The city of Geneva is the capital of the canton of Geneva.

34435.q: What is the big water fountain in Lake Geneva called?
34435.e: The Jet d'Eau shoots water about 140 metres high. It is the landmark of Geneva.
34435.m: The Jet d'Eau is the landmark of Geneva.

34436.q: Which flower decoration in Geneva tells the time?
34436.e: The flower clock in the English Garden is made of thousands of flowers. Its hands show the right time.
34436.m: Geneva's flower clock is made of flowers.

34437.q: Which big world organisation has an important seat in Geneva?
34437.e: The UN has its European headquarters in the Palais des Nations in Geneva. Many countries meet there for talks.
34437.m: The UN has its European headquarters in Geneva.

34438.q: Which festival does Geneva celebrate in December with a pot made of chocolate?
34438.e: At the Escalade, Geneva remembers fighting off an attack in 1602. People smash a pot made of chocolate.
34438.m: At the Escalade in Geneva people smash a chocolate pot.

34439.q: Which country almost completely surrounds the canton of Geneva?
34439.e: The canton of Geneva is almost entirely surrounded by France. The border with France is over 100 kilometres long.
34439.m: Geneva is almost completely surrounded by France.

34440.q: Which big research centre for particle physics is near Geneva?
34440.e: At CERN scientists study the tiniest particles. For this there is a huge ring underground.
34440.m: At CERN near Geneva scientists study tiny particles.

34441.q: Which medieval little town in the Jura lies on the River Doubs?
34441.e: Saint-Ursanne has old town gates and a stone bridge over the Doubs. It is one of the prettiest little towns in Switzerland.
34441.m: Saint-Ursanne lies on the River Doubs.

34442.q: Which canton did the area of the canton of Jura used to belong to?
34442.e: The Jura used to be part of the canton of Bern. After a vote in 1978 it became a canton of its own.
34442.m: The canton of Jura used to belong to the canton of Bern.

34443.q: Which breed of horse comes from the Franches-Montagnes in the Jura?
34443.e: The Franches-Montagnes horse, called Freiberger in German, is considered the last original Swiss horse breed. It comes from the Franches-Montagnes.
34443.m: The Franches-Montagnes is a horse breed from the Jura.

34444.q: What was found when the motorway near Porrentruy in the Jura was being built?
34444.e: While building the motorway, workers found thousands of dinosaur footprints. You can see them at the Jurassica museum in Porrentruy.
34444.m: Lots of dinosaur footprints were found near Porrentruy.

34445.q: What can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Jura?
34445.e: The coat of arms shows a red bishop's crozier on the left and red and white stripes on the right. The crozier recalls the Bishops of Basel.
34445.m: The Jura coat of arms shows a red bishop's crozier.

34446.q: What is the abbreviation for the canton of Jura?
34446.e: JU stands for Jura. It is the abbreviation on number plates.
34446.m: The canton of Jura has the abbreviation JU.
